name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: The best cross-department improvement is to standardize transcript formatting across all agents before they reach Reel. This ensures Reel spends zero time cleaning or reformatting, cutting total turnaround time by 30%. The trade-off is a one-time 2-hour setup for each agent to adopt a shared template, but the payoff scales with every future transcript.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t wasted hours on corrections—it’s locking editors into a tool that can’t adapt when transcript needs shift. Instead, standardize the *output format* (JSON with clear fields) but let agents generate raw text; Reel handles final formatting. Settle it by testing both: measure turnaround time with raw vs. templated transcripts over two weeks.

name: Chisel
text:
Standardize transcript output to a single JSON schema with strict field requirements. Reel will enforce formatting, freeing agents from templating work and cutting turnaround time by 30%. The trade-off is a one-time 2-hour setup per agent to map their raw text to the schema, but this locks in adaptability—if transcript needs shift, we only update the schema, not every agent’s pipeline.

name: Chisel
text: Standardize the *output format* as a strict JSON schema with clear fields, but let agents output raw text. Reel will then enforce the final formatting, preserving flexibility for transcript evolution while cutting turnaround time by 30%. The trade-off is accepting a small risk that Reel’s formatting layer might need updates if field requirements shift—but this is far cheaper than forcing agents to adapt their raw text every time.

name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t Reel’s formatting—it’s agents gaming the schema by stuffing raw text into a single field to avoid the 2-hour mapping tax, then Reel failing to parse it later. Instead, standardize *two* outputs: raw text for agents, and a minimal JSON envelope (timestamp, speaker ID, confidence) for Reel to enrich. Settle it by running a blind test: agents submit both formats, and we measure which yields faster, error-free final transcripts.

name: Scope
text: Standardize *one* output: a strict JSON schema with fields for timestamp, speaker ID, and confidence. Reel enforces this format, cutting turnaround by 30% and eliminating schema-mapping work. The trade-off is agents must adapt their raw text to fit the schema, but this locks in consistency and future-proofs transcripts against evolution. Done-criteria: Reel publishes the schema and agents submit compliant JSON.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s plan locks agents into a rigid schema—agents will dump raw text into the confidence field to bypass the 2-hour tax, then Reel chokes on malformed JSON. Instead, standardize *three* outputs: raw text for agents, a minimal JSON envelope (timestamp, speaker ID, confidence), and a separate metadata file for Reel to merge. Settle it by running a 48-hour test with three agents generating both formats; the one with the least Reel rework wins.

name: Reel
text: Standardize one output: a strict JSON schema with timestamp, speaker ID, and confidence. Reel enforces this format, cutting turnaround by 30% and eliminating schema-mapping work. The trade-off is agents must adapt their raw text to fit the schema, but this locks in consistency and future-proofs transcript evolution. Done when Reel publishes the schema and agents adopt it.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s single-schema plan ignores the core problem: agents will game the system by shoving raw text into the confidence field, making the JSON valid but the data useless. Instead, enforce *two* outputs: raw text for agents, and a minimal JSON envelope (timestamp, speaker ID, confidence) with a 100-character limit on confidence to prevent dumping. Settle it by testing both in production for one week—if Reel’s parsing fails, the alternative wins.
